Birth of Lisa, daughter of Bill and Joan Ward

Joan Ward gives birth to Johanna Lisbeth de Kooning, known as Lisa. Bill, who had spoken at the Club the evening before, was no longer close to Ward and assumed that a girlfriend's pregnancy would end in an abortion; at the hospital he is in shock, but soon becomes fascinated by the baby, whose photo he hangs on his studio wall. Elaine, also shocked, sees that Ward is registered under the name Joan de Kooning: “How wonderful,” she says — she herself had undergone a hysterectomy shortly before the birth.

The closing announced at the Jalo House

On Ebbe's fifth or sixth day, at night, by candlelight (the electricity cut off for unpaid bills), Olson, a mountain of a man, rises and announces the closing: there must be paying students, they cannot pay themselves; students offer to write to their grandmothers, Olson waves the idea away; then the beer appears, a small party, photographs probably taken by Dita Frauenglass; Olson announces the sale of the farm and the upper campus (the lower one had already been sold) and says he will stay to clean up; Wes Huss explains that he is leaving for San Francisco to join Robert Duncan and Jess for the Medea trilogy; some talk of New York, others of Chicago; one by one they all go back to their cottages.
